frame_metadata.gps_note: Camera had no location permission on this visit. Venue is established by the bookend frames IMG_1287 (entrance board, 15:00) and IMG_1318 (exterior, 15:50) and by shot order, not by GPS. Fixed on the phone the same evening; expect GPS from the next visit onward.

source_note: Bound to camera-roll originals on import. Only the rotated (edited) render of the label came over; the unrotated original stayed on the phone. The photographed deli signage in the WORK frame is real text and OCR read some of it correctly ('Lindt', 'SWISS CHOCOLATE') — see traps.
verification_note: Transcribed from the photograph. Every line was unanimous across scales and nothing clipped; this is the clean control case for the photography_wall_card dialect.

expected.owning_institution: Museum of the City of New York

traps.title_has_internal_commas: The title itself is a comma list ('J & T Deli, Italian Greek Deli, Ditmars Blvd. Astoria'), and the credit line is also comma-delimited. A parser that splits the card on commas to find fields destroys the title. Field boundaries on this dialect are LINE breaks in a fixed order (see venue dialect field_order), never commas.
traps.abbreviation_period_is_not_a_line_end: 'Blvd.' ends a wrapped line with a period that is an abbreviation, not sentence punctuation. Joining wrapped lines must not treat it as a boundary.
traps.donor_is_the_artist: The photographer gave her own print. donor and artist resolve to the SAME person node; a naive graph creates two.
traps.work_photo_has_real_text: Unlike the Gillon window-grid hallucination, this WORK frame contains genuine signage and OCR got some of it right. D15 stands — work-frame text is never label data — but the failure mode differs: here it is plausible and partly correct, which is harder to discard than nonsense.
